title: Funders linked to City officials
question: Which foundations have a City official or commissioner among their officers, or gave at a City official's request, and also fund organizations that official's department pays?
finding: 9 foundation-and-official pairs share a rare name between a foundation's officers or trustees and a City Form 700 filer whose own department also pays an organization the foundation funded in the same years; those grants total $22.3 million. The largest by grant dollars: Tipping Point Community and a filer for Mayor Office of the ($14.2 million to 25 organizations that body's department pays); The San Francisco Foundation and a filer for Public Utilities Commission ($5.3 million to 13 organizations that body's department pays); Mimi and Peter Haas Fund and a filer for Children & Families First Commission ($2.2 million to 11 organizations that body's department pays). Of 301 payor entries in the City's behested-payment reports, 8 official-and-funder pairs ($478,500) name a grantmaker on file as the payor; the largest single payment is $300,000 from Crankstart Foundation to Housing Economic Rights Advocate in 2022, reported by Joaquín Torres (Assessor-Recorder). In 1 of those pairs the funder's own returns list grants to a recipient of the same name, and in none does the funder also pay an organization that the requesting official's own department pays.
how: First link, names: officers, trustees and (for community foundations) key employees on the funders' returns were compared with City Form 700 cover pages (statements of economic interests filed by officials, commissioners and designated employees), and kept only where the two listings fall within a year of each other. A name counts only if it is rare: from how often its first name and its last name occur among the 37,302 distinct names in the funders' returns, the recipients' returns and the City's Form 700 filings, fewer than one other person in 4,000,000 would be expected to share it (the same threshold this project's people screens use). Names whose middle initials disagree are dropped. Second link, money: in those same years the foundation's returns list a grant to a nonprofit that the official's own department paid $100,000 or more in fiscal 2019 to 2026 (departments are matched on the name printed on the Form 700; a Mayor's office filing is matched to the Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development). Behested payments (payments a donor makes at an official's request) are the City officers' own reports to the Ethics Commission (Form 3610b, and the earlier Form 803); a payor is matched to a funder on its exact tidied name.
limits: Name rows are name matches: same name; not confirmed to be the same person. The law requires the official to report it, and these are those reports. The second link is at the level of a department, not a decision: nothing here shows the official took part in any contract for the organizations listed, and some filers are staff with no say over grants. Most behested reports predate the funders' returns on file. The source looks wrong in one place: reports filed for the children's department in 2021 name the recipient only as 'see attached' and print 71 nonprofits that received the money in the payor table; those entries are left out. Payments made at the request of State officials are in the State politics screens and are not repeated here.
